newsitem.title: MEXICO: Three Mexican miners killed in overnight explosion.
newsitem.headline: Three Mexican miners killed in overnight explosion.

text.p: An explosion ripped through a remote mine in western Mexico, killing three workers in the early hours of Tuesday, authorities said.

Three other nightshift workers at the small-scale San Isidro de Tepalcatepec barite mine in the western state of Michoacan escaped unharmed, Juan Lara Saenz, an official with the local public prosectutor's office, told Reuters.
Only six people were working on the overnight shift in the mine at the time of the blast, Lara said, adding the mine belonged to the privately held company Baricosta.
First indications were that the miners killed had misplaced explosives in an underground shaft in the mine that is around 240 miles (400 km) west of Mexico City.
"According to versions of other employees that were at the scene, it could have been caused by a misplacement of explosives," Lara added.
The mine is just across the border of Jalisco state, where Guadalajara is the state capital.
Initial reports from national TV network Televisa said the mine produced iron ore but Lara said it was worked for barite.
Barite is a colourless or white mineral used as a source for barium. One barium type is often administered to medical patients to help X-ray diagnosis.
